newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Aeroflot mulls 2nd weekly flight to Faro.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot mulls 2nd weekly flight to Faro.

text.p: Russian state airline Aeroflot may start operating a second weekly flight between Moscow and Faro in the tourist Algarve region in southern Portugal, its marketing director in Lisbon, Joaquim Ayres, said on Tuesday.
Aeroflot began operating a weekly flight between the two cities on June 13, after finding that many passengers on its Lisbon flights were travelling on to the Algarve.

Aeroflot uses the 183-seat Airbus A-310 aircraft on its Faro route. It was considering using the Ilyushin IL-86 or IL-96 aircraft, which have a capacity of more than 300 passengers, for a second weekly flight, Ayres told Reuters.

He added that the Ilyushin planes had been used on Aeroflot's Lisbon route when demand had surpassed the capacity of the airline's twice-weekly Tupolev TU-154 flights. TU-154s can carry a maximum of 132 passengers.

Ayres described Russian tourist interest in Portugal as a "boom". He said demand had been held back by delays in granting visas at the Portuguese embassy in Moscow, which had led some Russian tourists to opt for Spain instead.
Any changes to Aeroflot's Faro and Lisbon routes were likely to take effect from April or May next year, he said.
